guide.description: cut pulls one field out of delimiter-separated text — the tool of choice for CSV-shaped data where awk's whitespace splitting won't work. -d sets the delimiter, -f picks the field number (1-indexed, just like awk's $N). Write the delimiter right after -d with no quotes or space — this shell's tokenizer only strips quote characters when they open a word, so -d',' keeps its literal quote marks instead of stripping down to a comma.

flags.desc: the delimiter character to split on — no quotes, no space before it

examples.note: the 2nd comma-separated field of every line
